At its widest, in the mid-1950s, the gap was roughly 45 to 50 percentage points. In Gallup's 1956 polling, about 14% of Southerners approved of Black and white children attending the same schools, against roughly 60% or more in the rest of the country. The gap then narrowed steadily, and by the 1990s approval was near-universal in both regions. I'm working from memory of the Gallup trend figures, so the exact numbers may be off by a few points.

CONFIDENCE: 55
